title: Stream lifecycle: client ack debounce and coordinated server timeout orchestration (OpenAI compat)
author: Marco Reyes
release_notes: Backend: coordinate client-ack debounce with server idle timeout to reduce unnecessary model cancellations and improve reconnect/resume reliability. Improved observability metrics for stream lifecycle.
description: Motivation: we observed a class of incidents where rapid client reconnects or quick client-side cancels would cause the serving runtime to aggressively cancel in-flight model work, leading to wasted GPU work, transient 5xx errors surfaced to users, and degraded streaming UX. This PR introduces a coordinated lifecycle control that combines a client-ack debounce window with an explicitly negotiated server-side idle timeout and backpressure signal. High level: (1) client-side: introduce an ACK debounce period before the client-initiated cancel is treated as final; short disconnects within the debounce window are considered transient and eligible for resume; (2) server-side: connection_manager exposes an advisory idle_timeout that is negotiated per-session based on model latency profile and route SLO; (3) protocol: OpenAI-compat streaming adapter adds a small handshake field (x-rw-stream-lifecycle) to carry debounce and timeout hints when supported; (4) observability: new metrics for debounce_count, resume_success_rate, and lifecycle_cancellations. Implementation notes: kept changes localized to openai_adapter/streaming.py and serving/runtime/connection_manager.py. Added integration tests simulating flapping clients, unit tests for debounce logic, and e2e harness scenario validating resumable KV-cache preservation vs cancellation. Rollout plan: feature flagged by default off. Start with internal canary for 2 services for 48 hours, then enable incrementally by route. If regressions detected, set feature flag to off which restores previous behavior instantly. Impact: reduces unnecessary model cancellations and GPU churn; slightly increases latency for explicit cancels during debounce window (configurable, default 250ms). See linked Linear items ENG-894 and ENG-902 for benchmark targets and config knobs.

Marco Reyes (2026-02-24): Plumbed route config via route_config.stream_lifecycle.debounce_ms with sensible default; added unit tests and a Console API hook (no UI changes required in this PR).

merge_outcome: merged via squash merge on 2026-03-01. Squash commit: squash! client-ack debounce + server timeout negotiation. Post-merge: feature flag 'stream_lifecycle_v1' created in Config Service and default off for all public routes.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in canary region via deploy console before enabling on production.
If resume_success_rate drops below 95% for a model route, roll back feature flag immediately.
testing_summary: Added unit tests covering debounce FSM transitions, mocked connection_manager negotiation paths; added integration flappy-client test which asserts KV cache remains intact for reconnects within debounce window; synthetic perf harness shows decreased GPU cancellations. Tests exercised both OpenAI-compat header present and absent cases to ensure graceful fallback to prior behavior.
documentation_changes: Added docs/openai_compat/stream-lifecycle.md describing the handshake semantics, default debounce_ms=250, server idle advisory behavior, and recommended rollout steps. Updated examples/reconnect_kv_cache_example.py showing client reconnect flow using the debounce acknowledgement. Console documentation stub added for route-level config.
changelog_entry: Stability: coordinated client ack debounce and server idle timeout negotiation to reduce unnecessary cancellations and improve reconnect/resume reliability. Feature gated. See docs/openai_compat/stream-lifecycle.md for details.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: small added latency for explicit user cancels during the debounce window (default 250ms). Mitigation: route-configurable debounce_ms with immediate disable via feature flag; robust telemetry to detect regressions; start in canary for 48 hours.
